Arcane is a 6 -star character in Arknights: Endfield (AKE). Arcane wields an Arts Unit and belongs to the Caster class. Arcane also has access to the Nature element. sections.heading: Pros
sections.text:
2-in-1 unit, who can be played as a main DPS (INT form) or as an enabler (WILL form) to existing teams.

 Absurdly strong damage output on INT form, especially on the 2nd Ultimate cast, and top-class utility on WILL Form, be it grouping, debuffs or Inflictions.

 Capable of maintaining near constant Corrosion on enemies (which is buffed too!), ensuring maximum RES reduction at all times.

 Is that Longcat on her idle animation!?

sections.heading: Cons
sections.text:
Demands multiple gear sets to swap between INT and WILL forms, and can feel overly reliant on her Signature weapon for best performance.

 Need for 2 Final Strikes (or Finishers) to access her second Ultimate is cumbersome, slowing down rotations.

 Low Susceptibility duration is awkward to work around, where it’s easy to have it drop for critical bursts if not properly set-up.

 Shows that it is, in fact, possible to butt heads with Chen of all people.

sections.heading: Kit Intro
sections.text:
Arcane is a 6-star, Nature, Arts Unit Caster who introduces a brand new system to the game: the ability to swap forms based on her Attributes. All of her skills (with the exception of Basic Attack) have different functionality and even multipliers depending on whether Arcane’s INT or WILL is higher. If her INT is higher, then she takes on a main DPS role on a team, with high personal damage contribution and especially strong multipliers on her 2-part Ultimate. If her WILL is higher, then she takes on an enabler role, with additional effects like enemy grouping, stronger (and longer!) Susceptibility as well as the ability to duplicate Inflictions.
 Keep in mind that this form change does not alter her primary and secondary attributes! Any gear bonuses that increase “primary attribute” will always increase INT, and WILL is a much lower increase to her ATK than INT owing to it being a secondary attribute. Although this does reduce her damage when being run in WILL form, this is made up by additional effects, like a bonus to her Susceptibility the higher her WILL is.
 On top of this, Arcane also distinguishes herself from other operators by having an enhanced Corrosion. When combined with her ability to buff herself and debuff enemies alongside form specific bonuses, Arcane can fit in a large number of teams and be highly competitive no matter the scenario.

sections.heading: Talent
sections.text:
“ Tactical Planning ” is Arcane’s first Talent, and this is what determines what skills she uses. By default, it simply switches her “Array Arcana” - the skill type - depending on if her INT is >= her WILL and vice-versa.
 At level 2 however, it has additional effects to her Ultimate:
 For INT , it will give her a 24% Arts Amp buff during it. As her Ultimate is a 2-part skill, this can be active for skills that are cast between the first and second parts.

 For WILL , when her 1st or 2nd Ultimate deal damage, she inflicts Nature and Cryo Susceptibility for 10 seconds, up to 12.8%, with 0.02% per point of WILL. This means that Arcane needs at least 640 WILL to max out this buff!

 “ Weapon Honing ” is Arcane’s second talent, and it’s what makes her Corrosions so good: at max it will increase Corrosions applied by her by 10 seconds and makes it x1.1 times stronger.
 This is strictly Arcane ’s Corrosions. If another operator overwrites Arcane’s Corrosion, the duration extension will not carry over and it will refresh with a 15 second duration instead of 25.
 📝 Note

 Corrosion still retains the “highest” value of its RES reduction! If Arcane’s x1.1 Corrosion is weaker than that of another operator running Arts Intensity for example, her bonus will not carry over to the new Corrosion, as it would already be stronger regardless.

 A large part of Arcane's rotations is setting up a 4-stack Corrosion, then extending it indefinitely with multiple low-level Corrosions. This retains the high RES reduction value from the higher stack (and Arcane’s passive if applicable), while lasting long enough that it stays up for most of the team’s damage.
 As it lasts so long, the Corrosion is also constantly at max value, with no ramp-up needed if refreshed, making for an incredibly strong buff to both her personal damage in INT and team damage in WILL.

sections.heading: Basic Attack
sections.text:
“ Artillery Interdiction ” is Arcane’s Basic Attack, and it is the only skill in her kit that does not change depending on her form.
 It’s a standard 5-part string, both recovering 17 SP and dealing 17 stagger. Basic 3 can be animation cancelled, but there’s no meaningful gain in doing so.
 It isn’t all that noteworthy generally, being about average across the board. In INT form teams, as Arcane is likely to be the best built operator for general damage (unlike a Tangtang on Bonekrusha with Battle Skill DMG %), she is often the preferable controlled operator, which means this skill does see use.
 In WILL form teams however, other operators will have priority, both owing to being built for damage and due to additional effects (e.g. Yvonne Final Strike shortcutting or Last Rite’s fast Basic Attack cycling with animation cancels).

sections.heading: Battle Skill
sections.text: “ Jadecrushing Grid ” is Arcane’s Battle Skill, and regardless of what form she’s in, casting it will apply a Nature Infliction and deal some damage. This does have different form bonuses however:

sections.heading: INT form:
sections.text: Deals additional damage when cast, having a multiplier of 500% instead of 300%.

sections.heading: WILL form:
sections.text:
Pulls in enemies in a wide area to the centre of the skill.

 Both are straightforward, but the range and speed of this skill makes the grouping effect especially useful on WILL form.

sections.heading: Combo Skill
sections.text: “ Yinglung Stance IV ” is Arcane’s Combo Skill, and it sees significant changes across forms.

sections.heading: INT form:
sections.text:
Trigger requires a Nature Infliction or 2-stacks of non-Nature Arts Inflictions to be applied on an enemy, with a 12 second cooldown.

 It applies 4% Nature and Cryo Susceptibility to enemies for 4 seconds.

 Enemies have the “Imprisonment” effect applied, slowing their movement for 4 seconds.

 When Imprisonment ends, an additional volley of damage will be fired by clones at the enemy for extra damage and stagger.
 If a Battle Skill lands before the 4 seconds from Imprisonment expire, it will forcefully end it early, but deal additional damage, return 30 SP and replace (not extend!) the Susceptibility effect with another matching its value and lasting 3 seconds.

 📝 Note

 By “replace”, that means that if a Battle Skill lands after 2 seconds have passed, the total Susceptibility duration would be 5 seconds (2 seconds from cast, then 3 from the replaced instance). If it lands just before it expires at 4 seconds, then it could last up to 7 seconds (4 from the cast, then 3 from the replaced instance).

 In short, this skill gives a short-lived Susceptibility effect and, where possible, should be “detonated” early with a Battle Skill cast for the damage and SP return.
 As the Susceptibility duration is rather short, weaving this skill right before an Ultimate cast is ideal to maximise damage.

sections.heading: WILL form:
sections.text:
Trigger requires any Arts Infliction being applied on an enemy, with an 18 second cooldown.

 It applies 4% Nature and Cryo Susceptibility to enemies for 6 seconds, but this can be enhanced by 8% (to 12% total), scaling with WILL.
 640 WILL in total is required to max out the effect.

 Enemies have the “Imprisonment” effect applied, slowing their movement for 6 seconds.
 Imprisoned enemies will also be partially pulled into the centre of the skill.

 When Imprisonment ends, an additional volley of damage will be fired by clones at the enemy for extra damage and stagger.

 Unlike INT form, this one cannot be ended early, but has a longer base Susceptibility effect - both in damage and duration. As its effectively a “free” Infliction every 18 seconds, it is incredibly strong, and can significantly accelerate rotations on the teams Arcane is a part of.

sections.heading: Ultimate
sections.text:
“ Gloompurge ” is Arcane’s Ultimate, and most of its functionality is similar across both forms:
 On cast, it will immediately deal a burst of damage and set-up a “Gloompurger Array”. Every Finisher or Final Strike by the controlled operator will then trigger a “Cluster Strike”, up to 2 times.
 It’s only once 2 Cluster Strikes have activated that the second Ultimate, “Gloompurger Arcana” is unlocked, dealing a hefty burst of damage on cast.
 📝 Note

 During the period between the first and second Ultimates, Arcane will not build any Energy!

 Depending on the form, it has additional effects:

sections.heading: INT form:
sections.text:
The 24% Arts Amp effect from Arcane’s Tactical Planning Talent activates, with all skills used by her between the first and second casts being buffed.

 On cast, the Gloompurger Array applies forced Corrosion to all enemies in range.

 Gloompurger Arcana has significantly enhanced multipliers, up to 1440% at M3.

 The bulk of Arcane’s damage is loaded on her Ultimate: be the Array, Cluster Strikes or Arcana, maximising buff and debuff uptimes around them is very important. The Finisher/Final Strike requirement can be awkward to work with at times, but make sure that the Arcana portion lands in stagger where possible.

sections.heading: WILL form:
sections.text:
The up to 12.8% Nature and Cryo Susceptibility effect that scales with WILL from Arcane’s Tactical Planning Talent activates, lasting 10 seconds after the Gloompurger Array and Arcana deal damage.

 On cast, the Gloompurger Array will duplicate an existing Arts Infliction stack on enemies in range.

 Unlike the INT form, Arcane’s WILL Ultimate is mostly for its utility. As the Infliction duplication effect happens on cast, there can be scenarios where even if the Arcana portion is unlocked quickly, holding back until the 10 seconds Susceptibility have elapsed to reapply it after can be best. In practice, most enemies are dying shortly after (in fact killing enemies without relying on the second cast can be best for fast clears, owing to time spent in the Ultimate cutscene!), so when to use the Arcana cast can vary from team to team.

sections.heading: Energy
sections.text:
Arcane’s Ultimate Energy cost of 100 is very steep for her INT form, but her frequent Combo Skill uses can help make up for this. Keep in mind that as Arcane returns 30 SP to get the additional effects on her Combo Skill, this increases her Energy Gain Efficiency demands.
 This is even more important when considering that some of the teammates she’s likely to run with - like Tangtang - also have SP return effects, further reducing the total amount of Energy in a rotation.

sections.heading: How to Play
sections.text:
Arcane has 2 distinct playstyles that change depending on what form she’s using.
 For INT form, as the majority of her damage is loaded on Ultimate, setting up for the most damage during it is the priority.
 This will usually involve building 4 Arts Infliction stacks, then using her Battle Skill to apply a 4-stack Corrosion, then building up on Energy for her Ultimate. After which, work the rotation in such a way that teammate buffs/debuffs alongside a Combo Skill can be used prior to the second Ultimate, Gloompurge Arcana cast goes off so as to maximise its damage.
 The rotation will often follow:
 Apply 2 stacks of an Arts Infliction

 Use Arcane’s Combo Skill, but do not use her Battle Skill

 Apply another 2 stacks of the same Arts Infliction

 Use Arcane’s Combo Skill and “detonate” it with her Battle Skill for the additional effects

 Apply another 2 stacks of an Arts Infliction

 Use Arcane’s Combo Skill, after which Ultimate should be ready, and upon use this refreshes Corrosion

 Make use of the personal Amp effect while Ultimate is ready to fit in a Battle Skill to detonate her Combo Skill and begin landing Final Strikes/Finishers

 Once her second Ultimate is ready, make sure to trigger one more Combo Skill before use for its Susceptibility effect, then unload

 If needed and SP allows for it, make use of her Battle Skill before using the second Ultimate to squeeze in some extra damage

 The raw damage that she can dish out is likely enough to clear any encounter in a single rotation.
 The only weakness she has is low stagger build and the need for multiple Final Strikes/Finishers before using the second Ultimate, which does slow down things somewhat, but it does have a silver lining as it means Arcane’s burst is accommodating of multiple stagger thresholds (320, 340, etc.) as all that really matters is getting her Ultimate Cluster Strikes and Arcana hits before a stagger ends.
 As for WILL form, her exact value to a team can range on how she’s built and the exact comp that is being used.
 Yvonne for example, benefits greatly from the free Inflictions that Arcane can provide. Although her Ultimate Energy thresholds remain the same, Arcane allows for very comfortable SP positive rotations while providing more frequent and long lasting buffs, especially with her Ultimate’s Susceptibility.
 A Last Rite team on the other hand, isn’t as limited by SP and Cryo Infliction application, so it may be worthwhile to give up a 3+ stack Combo Skill on Last Rite early on and instead make use of it to apply a 4-stack Corrosion, exploiting the higher multiplier that she has on its effect for an even stronger RES reduction.
 The only important aspect of Arcane’s gameplan routing in WILL form is to work around her Combo Skill’s rather short Susceptibility period. As it lasts only 6 seconds, try to time it around ally bursts, stacking it with the bonus application from her Ultimate and Talent to get the most damage out.

 Type 42: Solemn Phalanx (P 0 )

 Arcane gets a tremendous amount of value from her Signature weapon, both for INT and WILL forms. The 46.4% Ultimate Gain Efficiency in line 2 is almost mandatory for INT form rotations and opens up more condensed WILL form rotations even when SP return from teammates is a factor. sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
Cryo

 Xaihi Cryo
 
 Xaihi buff value is immense, and it just so happens that most of her kit is relevant to Nature, being the backbone of any INT form team.

 As she’s able to build Cryo stacks, the differing element is useful for setting up a Corrosion reaction by Arcane.

 Final Strike requirement for her Combo Skill is easy to meet, and Arcane’s own need for 2 Finishers or Final Strikes to unlock the second Ultimate syncs well with this.

 Xaihi’s Amp is saturated by INT form’s Ultimate buff and her Cryo DMG Talent doesn’t contribute to Arcane directly.


 Cryo

 Last Rite Cryo
 
 Arcane’s WILL form can build Cryo Inflictions so quickly and cheaply that it enables for either additional Last Rite Combo Skills, or 4-stack Corrosions for her burst.

 As the bulk of Arcane’s value is on Combo and Ultimate use, she does not take away from the SP spent on Last Rite’s own Battle Skill.

 Last Rite suffers significantly on multi-target scenarios, but Arcane has “free” grouping with her Combo Skill that doesn’t apply conflicting Inflictions.

 Corrosion rotations demand sacrifices on Last Rite Combo Skills and Arcane’s Combo Skill grouping pales in comparison to her Battle Skill, which applies a Nature Infliction.


 Cryo

 Yvonne Cryo
 
 The “free” Inflictions brought about by Arcane’s WILL form are especially useful to Yvonne, who historically has struggled with being SP-gated in her rotations.

 The long Susceptibility effect on Arcane’s Ultimate allows for all of Yvonne’s burst to benefit from its effect, unlike other operators (Gilberta) where only a part of her Ultimate/Finisher saw buffs.

 Imprisonment is a big help to avoiding all too common Final Strike misses on Yvonne, and Arcane’s grouping capability is very helpful.

 Arcane’s Combo Skill is very difficult to align with Yvonne’s Ultimate and its short duration means it can be difficult to get the most value out of it.


 Cryo

 Tangtang Cryo
 
 Tangtang has both readily accessible Cryo Inflictions through her Battle Skill, and can offer both strong buffs and high personal damage.

 In both INT and WILL forms, Arcane’s Susceptibility also applies to Cryo damage, and given Tangtang’s “sub-DPS” capacity, this helps her contribution.

 Corrosion is beneficial to Tangtang too, and being of a differing element makes it easy to set it up through Cryo stacks.

 SP return on her skills can lead to awkward Ultimate Energy breakpoints when Potentials are considered.


 Nature

 Gilberta Nature
 
 As most of INT form’s damage is loaded on the second Ultimate cast and the period leading up to it, Gilberta’s high Susceptibility on her own Ultimate cast gets a lot of mileage.

 The relatively strong stagger build that Gilberta offers through her Combo Skill helps make up for one of the biggest weaknesses of Arcane teams.

 With Gilberta’s Talent increasing Caster Ultimate Gain Efficiency, she can allow for different weapon/gear choices and different rotations.

 Building Gilberta for Arts Intensity means that her Corrosions are going to be stronger, making the multiplier increase from Arcane’s Talent worthless and complicating rotations.


 Electric

 Perlica Electric
 
 Perlica’s high Arts DMG Taken effect from her Electrification is especially easy to trigger and is a highly competitive buff to any Arts team.

 Being an Electric operator, she can use Stanza for a strong buff to Arcane’s INT form burst.

 Her benefits are mostly generic Arts ones, and her Electric element can conflict with other operators run in Arcane teams (Xaihi, Tangtang) and their own Inflictions.

 Pros & Cons

 Pros
 2-in-1 unit, who can be played as a main DPS (INT form) or as an enabler (WILL form) to existing teams.

 Absurdly strong damage output on INT form, especially on the 2nd Ultimate cast, and top-class utility on WILL Form, be it grouping, debuffs or Inflictions.

 Cons
 Demands multiple gear sets to swap between INT and WILL forms, and can feel overly reliant on her Signature weapon for best performance.

 Need for 2 Final Strikes (or Finishers) to access her second Ultimate is cumbersome, slowing down rotations.

 Low Susceptibility duration is awkward to work around, where it’s easy to have it drop for critical bursts if not properly set-up.

 Kit Intro
 Arcane is a 6-star, Nature, Arts Unit Caster who introduces a brand new system to the game: the ability to swap forms based on her Attributes. All of her skills (with the exception of Basic Attack) have different functionality and even multipliers depending on whether Arcane’s INT or WILL is higher. If her INT is higher, then she takes on a main DPS role on a team, with high personal damage contribution and especially strong multipliers on her 2-part Ultimate. If her WILL is higher, then she takes on an enabler role, with additional effects like enemy grouping, stronger (and longer!) Susceptibility as well as the ability to duplicate Inflictions.
 Keep in mind that this form change does not alter her primary and secondary attributes! Any gear bonuses that increase “primary attribute” will always increase INT, and WILL is a much lower increase to her ATK than INT owing to it being a secondary attribute. Although this does reduce her damage when being run in WILL form, this is made up by additional effects, like a bonus to her Susceptibility the higher her WILL is.
 On top of this, Arcane also distinguishes herself from other operators by having an enhanced Corrosion. When combined with her ability to buff herself and debuff enemies alongside form specific bonuses, Arcane can fit in a large number of teams and be highly competitive no matter the scenario.
 Talent
 “ Tactical Planning ” is Arcane’s first Talent, and this is what determines what skills she uses. By default, it simply switches her “Array Arcana” - the skill type - depending on if her INT is >= her WILL and vice-versa.
 At level 2 however, it has additional effects to her Ultimate:
 For INT , it will give her a 24% Arts Amp buff during it. As her Ultimate is a 2-part skill, this can be active for skills that are cast between the first and second parts.

 For WILL , when her 1st or 2nd Ultimate deal damage, she inflicts Nature and Cryo Susceptibility for 10 seconds, up to 12.8%, with 0.02% per point of WILL. This means that Arcane needs at least 640 WILL to max out this buff!

 “ Weapon Honing ” is Arcane’s second talent, and it’s what makes her Corrosions so good: at max it will increase Corrosions applied by her by 10 seconds and makes it x1.1 times stronger.
 This is strictly Arcane ’s Corrosions. If another operator overwrites Arcane’s Corrosion, the duration extension will not carry over and it will refresh with a 15 second duration instead of 25.
 📝 Note

 Corrosion still retains the “highest” value of its RES reduction! If Arcane’s x1.1 Corrosion is weaker than that of another operator running Arts Intensity for example, her bonus will not carry over to the new Corrosion, as it would already be stronger regardless.

 A large part of Arcane's rotations is setting up a 4-stack Corrosion, then extending it indefinitely with multiple low-level Corrosions. This retains the high RES reduction value from the higher stack (and Arcane’s passive if applicable), while lasting long enough that it stays up for most of the team’s damage.
 As it lasts so long, the Corrosion is also constantly at max value, with no ramp-up needed if refreshed, making for an incredibly strong buff to both her personal damage in INT and team damage in WILL.
 Basic Attack
 “ Artillery Interdiction ” is Arcane’s Basic Attack, and it is the only skill in her kit that does not change depending on her form.
 It’s a standard 5-part string, both recovering 17 SP and dealing 17 stagger. Basic 3 can be animation cancelled, but there’s no meaningful gain in doing so.
 It isn’t all that noteworthy generally, being about average across the board. In INT form teams, as Arcane is likely to be the best built operator for general damage (unlike a Tangtang on Bonekrusha with Battle Skill DMG %), she is often the preferable controlled operator, which means this skill does see use.
 In WILL form teams however, other operators will have priority, both owing to being built for damage and due to additional effects (e.g. Yvonne Final Strike shortcutting or Last Rite’s fast Basic Attack cycling with animation cancels).
 Battle Skill
 “ Jadecrushing Grid ” is Arcane’s Battle Skill, and regardless of what form she’s in, casting it will apply a Nature Infliction and deal some damage. This does have different form bonuses however:
 INT form:
 Deals additional damage when cast, having a multiplier of 500% instead of 300%.

 WILL form:
 Pulls in enemies in a wide area to the centre of the skill.

 Both are straightforward, but the range and speed of this skill makes the grouping effect especially useful on WILL form.
 Combo Skill
 “ Yinglung Stance IV ” is Arcane’s Combo Skill, and it sees significant changes across forms.
 INT form:
 Trigger requires a Nature Infliction or 2-stacks of non-Nature Arts Inflictions to be applied on an enemy, with a 12 second cooldown.

 It applies 4% Nature and Cryo Susceptibility to enemies for 4 seconds.

 Enemies have the “Imprisonment” effect applied, slowing their movement for 4 seconds.

 When Imprisonment ends, an additional volley of damage will be fired by clones at the enemy for extra damage and stagger.
 If a Battle Skill lands before the 4 seconds from Imprisonment expire, it will forcefully end it early, but deal additional damage, return 30 SP and replace (not extend!) the Susceptibility effect with another matching its value and lasting 3 seconds.

 📝 Note

 By “replace”, that means that if a Battle Skill lands after 2 seconds have passed, the total Susceptibility duration would be 5 seconds (2 seconds from cast, then 3 from the replaced instance). If it lands just before it expires at 4 seconds, then it could last up to 7 seconds (4 from the cast, then 3 from the replaced instance).

 In short, this skill gives a short-lived Susceptibility effect and, where possible, should be “detonated” early with a Battle Skill cast for the damage and SP return.
 As the Susceptibility duration is rather short, weaving this skill right before an Ultimate cast is ideal to maximise damage.
 WILL form:
 Trigger requires any Arts Infliction being applied on an enemy, with an 18 second cooldown.

 It applies 4% Nature and Cryo Susceptibility to enemies for 6 seconds, but this can be enhanced by 8% (to 12% total), scaling with WILL.
 640 WILL in total is required to max out the effect.

 Enemies have the “Imprisonment” effect applied, slowing their movement for 6 seconds.
 Imprisoned enemies will also be partially pulled into the centre of the skill.

 When Imprisonment ends, an additional volley of damage will be fired by clones at the enemy for extra damage and stagger.

 Unlike INT form, this one cannot be ended early, but has a longer base Susceptibility effect - both in damage and duration. As its effectively a “free” Infliction every 18 seconds, it is incredibly strong, and can significantly accelerate rotations on the teams Arcane is a part of.
 Ultimate
 “ Gloompurge ” is Arcane’s Ultimate, and most of its functionality is similar across both forms:
 On cast, it will immediately deal a burst of damage and set-up a “Gloompurger Array”. Every Finisher or Final Strike by the controlled operator will then trigger a “Cluster Strike”, up to 2 times.
 It’s only once 2 Cluster Strikes have activated that the second Ultimate, “Gloompurger Arcana” is unlocked, dealing a hefty burst of damage on cast.
 📝 Note

 During the period between the first and second Ultimates, Arcane will not build any Energy!

 Depending on the form, it has additional effects:
 INT form:
 The 24% Arts Amp effect from Arcane’s Tactical Planning Talent activates, with all skills used by her between the first and second casts being buffed.

 On cast, the Gloompurger Array applies forced Corrosion to all enemies in range.

 Gloompurger Arcana has significantly enhanced multipliers, up to 1440% at M3.

 The bulk of Arcane’s damage is loaded on her Ultimate: be the Array, Cluster Strikes or Arcana, maximising buff and debuff uptimes around them is very important. The Finisher/Final Strike requirement can be awkward to work with at times, but make sure that the Arcana portion lands in stagger where possible.
 WILL form:
 The up to 12.8% Nature and Cryo Susceptibility effect that scales with WILL from Arcane’s Tactical Planning Talent activates, lasting 10 seconds after the Gloompurger Array and Arcana deal damage.

 On cast, the Gloompurger Array will duplicate an existing Arts Infliction stack on enemies in range.

 Unlike the INT form, Arcane’s WILL Ultimate is mostly for its utility. As the Infliction duplication effect happens on cast, there can be scenarios where even if the Arcana portion is unlocked quickly, holding back until the 10 seconds Susceptibility have elapsed to reapply it after can be best. In practice, most enemies are dying shortly after (in fact killing enemies without relying on the second cast can be best for fast clears, owing to time spent in the Ultimate cutscene!), so when to use the Arcana cast can vary from team to team.

 How to Play
 Arcane has 2 distinct playstyles that change depending on what form she’s using.
 For INT form, as the majority of her damage is loaded on Ultimate, setting up for the most damage during it is the priority.
 This will usually involve building 4 Arts Infliction stacks, then using her Battle Skill to apply a 4-stack Corrosion, then building up on Energy for her Ultimate. After which, work the rotation in such a way that teammate buffs/debuffs alongside a Combo Skill can be used prior to the second Ultimate, Gloompurge Arcana cast goes off so as to maximise its damage.
 The rotation will often follow:
 Apply 2 stacks of an Arts Infliction

 Use Arcane’s Combo Skill, but do not use her Battle Skill

 Apply another 2 stacks of the same Arts Infliction

 Use Arcane’s Combo Skill and “detonate” it with her Battle Skill for the additional effects

 Apply another 2 stacks of an Arts Infliction

 Use Arcane’s Combo Skill, after which Ultimate should be ready, and upon use this refreshes Corrosion

 Make use of the personal Amp effect while Ultimate is ready to fit in a Battle Skill to detonate her Combo Skill and begin landing Final Strikes/Finishers

 Once her second Ultimate is ready, make sure to trigger one more Combo Skill before use for its Susceptibility effect, then unload

 If needed and SP allows for it, make use of her Battle Skill before using the second Ultimate to squeeze in some extra damage

 The raw damage that she can dish out is likely enough to clear any encounter in a single rotation.
 The only weakness she has is low stagger build and the need for multiple Final Strikes/Finishers before using the second Ultimate, which does slow down things somewhat, but it does have a silver lining as it means Arcane’s burst is accommodating of multiple stagger thresholds (320, 340, etc.) as all that really matters is getting her Ultimate Cluster Strikes and Arcana hits before a stagger ends.
 As for WILL form, her exact value to a team can range on how she’s built and the exact comp that is being used.
 Yvonne for example, benefits greatly from the free Inflictions that Arcane can provide. Although her Ultimate Energy thresholds remain the same, Arcane allows for very comfortable SP positive rotations while providing more frequent and long lasting buffs, especially with her Ultimate’s Susceptibility.
 A Last Rite team on the other hand, isn’t as limited by SP and Cryo Infliction application, so it may be worthwhile to give up a 3+ stack Combo Skill on Last Rite early on and instead make use of it to apply a 4-stack Corrosion, exploiting the higher multiplier that she has on its effect for an even stronger RES reduction.
 The only important aspect of Arcane’s gameplan routing in WILL form is to work around her Combo Skill’s rather short Susceptibility period. As it lasts only 6 seconds, try to time it around ally bursts, stacking it with the bonus application from her Ultimate and Talent to get the most damage out.

As for WILL form, it increases the Susceptibility bonus by 7% and is an immediate 30% cut to her Combo Skill’s cooldown after using Gloompurge Arcana. It is better for INT, as most enemies are dead within a single rotation anyways, but WILL form could see greater benefits on more extended encounters (like Contingency Contract), and when paired with P4's cost reduction, could open up new rotations too.

 Teams and Synergies

 Synergies

 Cryo

 Xaihi Cryo
 
 Xaihi buff value is immense, and it just so happens that most of her kit is relevant to Nature, being the backbone of any INT form team.

 As she’s able to build Cryo stacks, the differing element is useful for setting up a Corrosion reaction by Arcane.

 Final Strike requirement for her Combo Skill is easy to meet, and Arcane’s own need for 2 Finishers or Final Strikes to unlock the second Ultimate syncs well with this.

 Xaihi’s Amp is saturated by INT form’s Ultimate buff and her Cryo DMG Talent doesn’t contribute to Arcane directly.


 Cryo

 Last Rite Cryo
 
 Arcane’s WILL form can build Cryo Inflictions so quickly and cheaply that it enables for either additional Last Rite Combo Skills, or 4-stack Corrosions for her burst.

 As the bulk of Arcane’s value is on Combo and Ultimate use, she does not take away from the SP spent on Last Rite’s own Battle Skill.

 Last Rite suffers significantly on multi-target scenarios, but Arcane has “free” grouping with her Combo Skill that doesn’t apply conflicting Inflictions.

 Corrosion rotations demand sacrifices on Last Rite Combo Skills and Arcane’s Combo Skill grouping pales in comparison to her Battle Skill, which applies a Nature Infliction.


 Cryo

 Yvonne Cryo
 
 The “free” Inflictions brought about by Arcane’s WILL form are especially useful to Yvonne, who historically has struggled with being SP-gated in her rotations.

 The long Susceptibility effect on Arcane’s Ultimate allows for all of Yvonne’s burst to benefit from its effect, unlike other operators (Gilberta) where only a part of her Ultimate/Finisher saw buffs.

 Imprisonment is a big help to avoiding all too common Final Strike misses on Yvonne, and Arcane’s grouping capability is very helpful.

 Arcane’s Combo Skill is very difficult to align with Yvonne’s Ultimate and its short duration means it can be difficult to get the most value out of it.


 Cryo

 Tangtang Cryo
 
 Tangtang has both readily accessible Cryo Inflictions through her Battle Skill, and can offer both strong buffs and high personal damage.

 In both INT and WILL forms, Arcane’s Susceptibility also applies to Cryo damage, and given Tangtang’s “sub-DPS” capacity, this helps her contribution.

 Corrosion is beneficial to Tangtang too, and being of a differing element makes it easy to set it up through Cryo stacks.

 SP return on her skills can lead to awkward Ultimate Energy breakpoints when Potentials are considered.


 Nature

 Gilberta Nature
 
 As most of INT form’s damage is loaded on the second Ultimate cast and the period leading up to it, Gilberta’s high Susceptibility on her own Ultimate cast gets a lot of mileage.

 The relatively strong stagger build that Gilberta offers through her Combo Skill helps make up for one of the biggest weaknesses of Arcane teams.

 With Gilberta’s Talent increasing Caster Ultimate Gain Efficiency, she can allow for different weapon/gear choices and different rotations.

 Building Gilberta for Arts Intensity means that her Corrosions are going to be stronger, making the multiplier increase from Arcane’s Talent worthless and complicating rotations.


 Electric

 Perlica Electric
 
 Perlica’s high Arts DMG Taken effect from her Electrification is especially easy to trigger and is a highly competitive buff to any Arts team.

 Being an Electric operator, she can use Stanza for a strong buff to Arcane’s INT form burst.

 Her benefits are mostly generic Arts ones, and her Electric element can conflict with other operators run in Arcane teams (Xaihi, Tangtang) and their own Inflictions.
